== History ==
Luritja people have inhabited the area for at least 20,000 years.
Ernest Giles was an early English explorer who reached the canyon in 1872.


=== Name ===
Kings Creek runs along the bottom of the canyon and gives it its name. The creek was named by Giles in 1872. He wrote in his book Geographic Travels in Central Australia from 1872 to 1874: "I called King's Creek after Mr. Fielder King... an old and kind friend of mine".
The Aboriginal (Luritja and Arrernte) name for the creek and canyon is "Watarrka" (pronounced what-ARR-kah), which is the Luritja word for the local umbrella bush (Acacia ligulata) that grows in the vicinity. The national park thus gets its name from this landform.


== Location, access, and description ==
